SECTION IX
CITIZEN PARTICIPATION & COMMUNITY ATTITUDES
A. CITIZEN PARTICIPATION
The CDBG Program was authorized by the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974. The Housing and Community Development Act of 1977 continues the CDBG for the other three years. The objectives and requirements of that Act will be similar to the previous CDBG legislation.
One requirement of the CDBG legislation is that jurisdictions applying for CDBG funding provide meaningful citizen participation in the development of the three year plan and program. This includes holding public hearings to (1) obtain views of citizens on community development and housing needs and priorities, and (2) review the proposed CDBG application prior to its adoption. The applicant is also required to adopt a citizen participation plan.
The City Council adopted such a plan on November 5, 1974. This plan involved active citizen participation in the CDBG program, including review and recommendations by a Community Development Block Grant Steering Committee and Community Development Activity Area Committees as well as at least two public hearings annually on the CDBG program. This structure worked very successfully over the past three years and has been expanded for the current CDBG program to detail the role of citizens in the initial planning process, program implementation, and program amendments and future planning.
Objectives 
The objectives of the proposed citizen participation process are:
1. To form a citizen participation structure which adheres to the provisions of the Act and represents the community development related groups, boards, and commissions in the city as well as residents of the Community Development Activity Areas.
2. To provide all residents of the target areas and other interested citizens with the opportunity to: 
(a) Define local needs
(b) Review program proposals
(c) Review and evaluate the plan
(d) Provide specific program recommendations
3. To provide adequate citizen involvement in all phases of the CDBG program including: 
(a) Development of a comprehensive strategy and determination of priorities
(b) Development and review of the Community Development Plan
(c) Review of subsequent amendments to the program, and
(d) Review of program implementation, monitoring and evaluation
